goal: Privacy repair (owner-authorized, new work, not retroactive): chongdae's public task records leak this machine's absolute paths (jokbo run-20261030-063525-2d81: stages.newbie.response.tried[].command). Contain first with machine-local commit-records:false in a recorded environment task; then the lock's Claude tests writer and Codex builder make save_state write a path-normalized public projection while exact raw values stay in ignored local state for validation, recovery and ownership; the lock's Claude verifier checks it. No version bump, push, cache change or history rewrite; prior README/AGENTS/manifest edits and SELFHOSTING.md stay as they are.
brief:
Build contract P2-rel (below) in chongdae.py only, on top of the accepted projection-build (commit 2fe1b61): the narrow projection that public_projection uses must replace a temporary-directory prefix only where it begins a path. neutral_path (narrow=False) and its existing callers keep their behavior exactly (a protected test pins neutral_path('src<tmp>') == 'src<tmp>'). Protected tests: test_public_projection.py (14 earlier tests + 5 test_P2_rel_*) and test_chongdae.py — do not change them. Do not touch README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, the three manifests, SELFHOSTING.md, hunsu.json or hunsu.lock.json (a check hashes them). No version bump, no new command/setting/key, do not commit. Note from the earlier attempts: a worker inheriting AGENT_WORKER=1 sees seven hook tests fail in the full suite; chongdae's own check run decides.

Contract P2-rel (amends P2 of contract P, which says relative paths are "unchanged byte for byte"). The session found, after projection-build was accepted, that the narrow projection still rewrites a relative path whose segment is named like a temporary directory: `src<tmp>` becomes `src<tmp>`, `.<tmp>` becomes `.<tmp>`, `build<tmp>` becomes `build<tmp>` (the temp rules have no left boundary). P2-rel: in the public projection (public files save_state writes, and public_projection), a temporary-directory prefix — tempfile.gettempdir() and its realpath, `/tmp`, `/private/tmp`, `/var/folders` — is replaced by `<tmp>` only where it begins a path: at the start of the string, or right after whitespace, a quote, a backtick, or one of = ( [ , : ; | & >. Everywhere else it is part of another path and stays unchanged: `src<tmp>`, `.<tmp>`, `tests/fixtures<tmp>`, `build<tmp>`, `a<tmp>`. Absolute temp paths at a path start still become `<tmp>`: `<tmp>`, `see <tmp>`, `--out=<tmp>`, `('<tmp>')`, `PATH=/usr/bin:<tmp>`. Raws stay exact in the overlay as P3 says. neutral_path itself (its existing callers: portable, asked/) is not changed by P2-rel.

Contract P: chongdae's public run records are a path-normalized projection; the exact raw values stay in ignored local state.

Context (verified by the session on this checkout, chongdae.py as released in 1.24.0): `save_state(d, state)` writes a run directory `d` (normally `<project>/.chongdae/run-<id>`): `tasks/<id>.json` (the public record, committed by `commit_record`), `local/tasks/<id>.json` (this machine's overlay of PRIVATE_KEYS; `local/` is git-ignored through `.chongdae/.gitignore`) and `state.json` (the run's own fields), all through one journal `local/state-transaction.json` (`recover_state(d)` replays a prepared generation). `load_state(d)` merges each public task with its overlay (`merge_private`). `split_private` moves only PRIVATE_KEYS (`session`, `transcript`, `commands`, `read`, ...) to the overlay, so every other string goes to the public file verbatim: a hired role's answer saved as `ts["stages"][role] = {"response": {...}, "by": {...}, "when": "after"}`, a failed one as `ts["stages"][role]["failed"] = [{"response": {...}, "by": {...}, "when": ...}]`, a builder's `ts["response"]`, earlier answers in `ts["attempts"]` (a list of response-shaped dicts), the verifier's review, `summary`, findings (`{"kind", "where", "quote", "why"}`), `non-claims`. Observed leak: jokbo's committed record run-20261030-063525-2d81 tasks/environment.json holds `stages.newbie.response.tried[0].command` = "mktemp -d <absolute project root>/newbie-environment.XXXXXX". `neutral_path(text, target)` already states the machine-path policy that `asked/` files use (through `portable`).

P1 Public files are projections. Every public JSON file save_state writes in a run directory — `tasks/<id>.json` and `state.json` — holds, for each string value at any depth (dict values and list items alike, including inside `response`, `attempts[]`, `stages.<role>.response`, `stages.<role>.failed[].response`, the review, findings, `summary`, `non-claims`), the string with this machine's path prefixes replaced: the project root (its abspath and its realpath) -> `.` (`<root>/x` -> `./x`), the home directory -> `~` (`<home>/x` -> `~/x`), a temporary directory (`tempfile.gettempdir()` and its realpath, `/tmp`, `/private/tmp`, `<tmp>`) -> `<tmp>` as neutral_path does it, and a host plugin cache path -> `<plugin:NAME@VERSION>` as neutral_path does it. The project root is the parent of the `.chongdae` directory that holds the run directory; a run directory not inside a directory named `.chongdae` has no project root, and only the other prefixes are replaced. The project root is replaced before the home and temp prefixes (a project under the home or under a temp directory becomes `.`, not `~/...` or `<tmp>`).

P2 Narrow: path prefixes only. The project root and the home are replaced only where they are a whole path prefix: followed by `/`, or ending the path (end of string, whitespace, a quote, or one of ` ; | & ) , :). `<home>-old/x` and `<root>2/x` are not under the home or the root and stay unchanged. neutral_path's bare account-name rule (`<user>`) is not applied: a string that holds the account name only as a word — a `--by` signature, an author line — is unchanged. Dict keys, non-string values, relative paths (`src/a.py`, `./x`, `README.md#versioning`), quotes with no absolute machine path, and actor metadata (`host`, `model`, `agent`, `by`, `effort`, `at`) are unchanged byte for byte. PRIVATE_KEYS keep going to the overlay unprojected, as today.

P3 Exact raw values stay local, in the same transaction. For every string P1 changed, the exact original stays in the run's ignored local state: the task's `local/tasks/<id>.json` overlay (for `state.json`: `local/state.json`), as a mirror `merge_private` restores, list items included (a raw string at a list index). The public file and its overlay are written in one `local/state-transaction.json` generation, so a process death between the two writes recovers both (recover_state) or neither. `load_state(d)` returns exactly what was given to `save_state` (apart from the `artifact-type`/`written_by` stamps save_state adds) — every string at any depth equal to its raw original — in this process and in a new process after a restart; validation, result consumption, verifier-quote checks, recovery, task ownership (`added-in`, lease keys) and generation guards keep reading that merged raw view.

P4 Originals untouched. Files under `local/` written by or for providers — the request as sent, `<tag>.response.json`, transcripts, logs — are never rewritten or reformatted by the projection: a response file's bytes (sha256) are the same before and after its answer is consumed into the task and saved. No answer's quote, finding or field is changed to pass validation.

P5 No projection-only rewrite of existing records. A public file whose raw content (the public file merged with its overlay) is unchanged by a save is not rewritten: a run written before this change, whose public task files hold absolute paths and have no raw overlay, keeps those files byte for byte when its state is loaded and saved without a change to that task. A save that changes a task writes that task's public file projected and its raws to the overlay. Old overlays (PRIVATE_KEYS only) load as before.

P6 Record commits carry only the projection. With `settings.chongdae.commit-records` not false, a record commit (`commit_record(target, run_name, message)`) after a save whose task holds absolute home/project/temp paths contains the projected public file (`git show HEAD:<run>/tasks/<id>.json` holds none of those absolute paths) and nothing under `local/`.

P7 A pure function for derived exports. `public_projection(obj, target)` returns `(public, raws)`: `public` is a copy of `obj` with P1/P2 applied to every string (`target` None: no project root), `raws` the mirror such that `merge_private(public, raws)` equals `obj`; it writes nothing and does not modify `obj`. save_state uses it. No CLI command, setting or record key is added.

P8 Suites. `python3 test_chongdae.py` exits 0: the existing suites (test_concurrency, test_review_freshness, test_record_transactions, test_launch_recovery, test_state_recovery, test_completion_recovery, test_mutation_ownership, test_operation_recovery, test_operation_handover) unchanged and passing, and the new suite `test_public_projection` in its `loadTestsFromNames` list.

projection-tests-rel: For the absolute examples, the tests check that the text before the path start is kept, that the result continues with '<tmp>', that no /tmp, /private/tmp or /var/folders is left, and that a closing "')" is kept. They do not pin down exactly what follows <tmp>, because the contract only says the prefix is "replaced by `<tmp>`" the way neutral_path does it.

Not every path-start character in the list ("whitespace, a quote, a backtick, or one of = ( [ , : ; | & >") gets its own test. Only the contract's own examples are covered: start of string, a space, '=', "('" and ':'.

The neutral_path test fixes the current behaviour (neutral_path('src<tmp>') == 'src<tmp>') because of the sentence "neutral_path itself (its existing callers: portable, asked/) is not changed by P2-rel". If that function's behaviour is ever changed on purpose, this test has to change too.

For the absolute examples, the tests check that the head before the path start is kept, that the result continues with '<tmp>', that no /tmp, /private/tmp or /var/folders is left after the head, and that a closing "')" is kept. They do not pin down exactly what follows <tmp>.

projection-tests: P8 has no test_P8 method. Its check is `python3 test_chongdae.py` exiting 0. A test that ran that command from inside the suite would call itself forever, and a test that only searched the file for the new list entry would already pass, because I added that entry. The entry itself is the one line I added to test_chongdae.py.

P3: "validation, result consumption, verifier-quote checks, recovery, task ownership (`added-in`, lease keys) and generation guards keep reading that merged raw view". Only part of this is tested: load_state returning raw values (including added-in and lease-held) and recovery. No test drives validation, result consumption or the verifier-quote checks through the CLI against projected records.

P3: "recovers both (recover_state) or neither". The "neither" half is not tested separately. The crash test interrupts the write of local/tasks/<id>.json through c.save_changed (the pattern in test_state_recovery.py) and requires the process to exit with 77. If the build writes the overlay some other way than save_changed, that test fails. Today it fails because the overlay never changes, so the crash point is never reached.
P4: "No answer's quote, finding or field is changed to pass validation" is not tested. No validation path is exercised.
P7: "No CLI command, setting or record key is added" is not tested. No test can list everything that was not added.

P1: the realpath of a temporary directory, and `<tmp>` paths, are checked only by being absent from the public file and by `<tmp>` appearing in it. The exact `<tmp>` form follows neutral_path and is not pinned to a literal string.

test_P2_only_whole_path_prefixes_and_metadata_unchanged briefly creates and removes a hidden `.teujip-projection-*` folder in the checkout. A temp directory cannot be the project there, because then `<root>2/x` would itself be a temp path.
